length.text: Up to about 1.8 m (tail about 0.6 m)

overview.text: The Asian Vine Snake is a very slender, often bright green tree snake of South and South-east Asia with a long, pointed snout. It is mildly venomous, with fangs at the back of its mouth.

identification.text: Extremely slender with a long, pointed snout more than twice as long as the eye. Light brown to yellow-green, often a startling bright green.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Up to about 1.8 m long, of which about 0.6 m is tail.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: From north-eastern India and Bangladesh through Myanmar, Thailand and Indochina to southern China, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and the Philippines.

diet.text: Small reptiles and amphibians, especially lizards and tree frogs.

reproduction.text: The Reptile Database lists it as giving birth to live young.

funfacts.text: It looks almost exactly like the vine snakes of South America, but they are not close relatives - they evolved the same shape for the same tree-top life.
